summary: An excerpt from a novel's Book 10 (part 143) following Leon, a meticulous man who consciously suppresses a childhood self nicknamed the "Hansel and Gretel" kid who left messes everywhere. His parents, who emigrated from Romania to Anguilla, teased his organization; he resists impulses toward indulgence and plans to sell something new to a wealthy man in a vat. The passage also describes the shifting Lower East Side neighborhood, where shops and buildings change with the economy, and recalls Leon's family's hardship after arriving in Anguilla during an economic collapse.
one_line: Leon, a rigidly disciplined man haunted by his messy childhood, reflects on his habits and the changing Lower East Side and his family's hardships.
key_facts: Leon routinely stops at the grocer's every night to buy anything that ran out the previous day.
His parents visited from Anguilla and teased him about how organized he was.
Leon's sixth grade teacher awarded him the "Hansel and Gretelprize" for leaving a trail behind him everywhere he went.
Leon denies his inner voice that calls for pizzas, sleeping in, and taking cabs, shouting it into submission and locking it up.
Leon plans to sell something new to the man in the vat, reasoning that a man who amassed a great fortune would have spent his life denying himself.
The Lower East Side has cycled through poor, rich, middle-class, super-rich, and poor phases over the years.
Leon sniffs change in the wind in his neighborhood: more discount high-calorie wino-drink, fewer designer low-carb energy foods, and more FOR RENT signs.
A construction site has had no one working on it for a week, and its padlocked foreman's shed is growing a mossy coat of graffiti.
Leon's parents emigrated from Romania to Anguilla, chasing the tax-haven set and dreaming of making a killing as bookkeepers or security guards.
Leon's parents arrived in Anguilla in the middle of an "econopocalyptic collapse" and ended up living in a vertical slum that had once been a luxury hotel.
The Romanians were the sole non-Mexican people among smuggled Mexicans who were de-facto slaves.
The passage notes that the advantage of de-facto slaves over de-jure slaves was that the text is cut off before finishing this thought.
